pageCache.text:
Welcome to John Henry Newman Academy!
John Henry Newman Academy, a GOOD primary school, in the heart of Littlemore, is a vibrant, happy and exciting place to be for children and their families. We are a two-form entry school for children aged between 3 and 11. The Academy serves the inner city of Oxford and the communities of Littlemore, Rosehill and Blackbird Leys.
We are a Church of England school, part of Oxford Diocesan School Trust, underpinned by our strong Christian ethos with well-established links with our local church, St Mary and St Nicholas. We welcome children and families from all faiths and backgrounds, and embrace the diverse community we have in Littlemore.
The first school in Littlemore was founded in 1830 by the 19th Century priest and poet John Henry Newman. There has been a church school in Littlemore ever since these beginnings. The Littlemore Infants School was sited on land donated by the owner of the Lawn Upton estate and built in 1903, it later became known as Speedwell School.
The new John Henry Newman CE Aided Primary school was built in 2002 on a wonderful history and tradition of primary education provided by the previous two schools. In 2012, the Governors opted to convert to academy status with the Diocese of Oxford as its sponsor, the first school as part of the newly created Multi Academy Trust.
You can read about us in the Oxford Mail:
Please come and see our wonderful school!
Executive Headteacher
“John Henry Newman Academy is warm and welcoming to all. Pupils enjoy being part of such a diverse and inclusive school community. They absolutely believe in the school’s vision – ‘let your light shine’. This belief permeates through the entire school community and forges the strong relationships within it.”
“Additional support is carefully structured to help all pupils succeed, including those who are disadvantaged. This means that all pupils access the full curriculum, with appropriate adaptations.”
“Pupils benefit from the school’s many meaningful relationships with the local community. One parent sums up the views of many when they say: ‘The school has helped my child to recognise the opportunities that lie ahead for them in the world, where anything is possible.’’’

Extra-Curricular Activities at JHN
AT the John Henry Newman Academy there are many opportunities for children to take part in regular extra curricular activities both during the school day and after school. We work with a number of people within the community to collaborate on and undertake larger projects. All of these projects and activities are opportunities for the children to enrich, develop and broaden through learning new skills, moving out of their comfort zones working as part of a team!
Keep a look out for updates on our whole school play Matilda. Auditions are well under way and we cannot wait to share our progress with you!
We will keep you updated with any fixtures and experiences on this page.
In Term 4 we will be running:
Year group/ Key Stage
Enjoy the chance to play a number of different games with Mr Surman, learning the rules all while having fun.
Join Mrs French to practice some phonics and enjoy some of our new and exciting books in the Librarium!
Join in with cooking club to learn the tricks of the trade from Miss Snell.
TT rockstars/ Numbots
Miss Coombs & Miss Powell
Work with our knowledgeable staff to practice your times tables and number bonds in a calm and supportive environment.
Enjoy the chance to play a number of different games with Mr Surman, learning the rules all while having fun.
Mrs Corris & Miss Padbury
Join Mrs Corris and Miss Padbury, our resident singing superstars to prepare for some exciting upcoming performances
If you would like your child to join one of these extra-curricular activities, please register your interest on MCAS (My child at school app) and we will let you know if you have been successful by the end of each term.
Each after school activity runs until 4pm (unless otherwise stated) and collection will be either at the bottom gate or outside the school office.
Check out our ‘Sports‘ page to see when upcoming fixtures are, where they are being held and how well they are getting on!

pageCache.pageTitle: Home Learning Resources – John Henry Newman Academy
pageCache.text:
At John Henry Newman Academy, we believe that learning at home is an essential part of a child’s education. It offers a unique opportunity for children to explore new ideas, practise important skills, and showcase the fantastic learning they do at school in the comfort and safety of their own home. By working as a team—parents, children, and teachers together—we can highlight the value of learning and help children develop a love for it that lasts a lifetime.
We do not issue weekly homework but instead focus on building fluency at home. Reading is at the heart of this approach. We encourage you to read with your child every day, whether that’s sharing a bedtime story, exploring books sent home from school, or even reading real-world materials like recipes or instructions.
As children progress through the school, they will begin to learn spelling rules and techniques that require weekly practice. To support this, we provide short clips available on our website and social media to guide you through fun and effective ways to help your child.
Maths skills are equally important, and we use Timestables Rockstars and Numbots to make practising number bonds and multiplication tables engaging and fun. These online tools help children build confidence in their arithmetic and problem-solving abilities through independent play and should be completed weekly.
Each term, children will also complete a few activities as part of their ‘Mini Duke of Edinburgh’ programme. These tasks, shared on Tapestry and the class pages, are designed to encourage creativity, independence, and teamwork. Families can upload their progress to Tapestry, and these achievements will be recorded in the children’s Mini Duke of Edinburgh booklets. An after-school club is also available to support children in completing these exciting challenges.
For more resources, activity ideas, and helpful guides to make home learning easier and more enjoyable, please explore the links provided on this page. Together, we can create a supportive and inspiring environment where every child can thrive.

Timestables Rockstars
Times Tables Rock Stars is an award-winning maths learning platform where children can practise their times tables like a rock star!
Suitable for all learners aged 6 years and up, our question-based games automatically adapt to each child’s unique learning needs, helping them to recall their times tables in record speed. Accessible on any device, via the app or browser, children can play anytime, anywhere. Plus, the engaging gamification and motivating rewards mean it is never difficult to entice children to play. Result!
Times Tables Rock Stars boosts maths confidence and incresaes fluency and recall in multiplication and division, delivering better maths outcomes. It adapts to each user’s unique learing needs and allows us to track their individual progress. Kids love earning virtual coins to personliase their rock avatars and move up the rock leaderboard from “New Artist” to “Hero”.
Please speak to your child’s calss teacher if you do not know your child’s login details.
Please click this link to go to the Timestables Rock Stars website.
FFT Phonics
At JHN we are very lucky to work with FFT to help with our early reading, phonics and Spelling, Punctuation and Grammar for chidlren across the school. FFT also have a very helpful Parent Portal which provides information on:
Our JHN Passcode is: FFTJHN
Phonics and Writing phases
Oxford Reading Buddy
Dear Parents/Carers,
We are really excited to provide every child with a login for Oxford Reading Buddy. It is accessible on any device to develop children’s reading development at home as well as at school.
Oxford Reading Buddy contains hundreds of digital books and book-quizzes all matched to each child’s reading ability. Children can earn badges for good reading behaviours, be coached in their understanding by their personal ‘Reading Buddy’, take quizzes and record all the reading they do. Everything is captured so that your child’s teacher can see how they’re getting on.
Please log in with your child when your child brings home their sign-in card and have a look around. (Or speak to the office or your child’s class teacher if you need it again). Do encourage your child to use it regularly and discuss what they are reading with them. The John Henry Newman Academy Nursery takes children from the term after they turn 3. Places will be for September, January or April for children to start.
We offer a morning session from 8:45 -11:45 and afternoon sessions from 12 -3pm. We also offer full time places at a small fee. Children staying all day can also have a delicious hot lunch cooked by the school kitchen.
We have spacious attractive, stimulating and fun indoor and outdoor space. The nursery is highly equipped to provide a caring and nurturing environment for your child as they take their first exciting steps into education.
Ofsted (June 2018) have commented that ‘The early years is well led. Children have good opportunities to flourish across a wide range of curriculum areas and are kept safe’.

Governance Structure
Our Governors provide strategic leadership and accountability in our school. Governors appoint the Head of School and the Assistant Headteachers. The Executive Headteacher was appointed by the Governors and ODST. It is governors who hold senior leaders to account for the performance of the school and, working with the Executive Headteacher, make the tough decisions about balancing resources.
ODST has a Board of Trustees which oversees the work of the Trust including the effectiveness of Local/Joint Governing Bodies.
As of September 2025, our Governing Board officially became a joint governing board with St Christopher’s Primary School in Cowley (SCC).
Our Joint Governing Board meets up to six times a year. Every governor attends these meetings and may also be a member of our sub-committee, which meet circa five times a year.
The Resources Committee ensures that the school uses its resources to achieve best value, thereby supporting the learning of all our students. This Committee is also responsible for Health and Safety, Premises and Staffing.
